messages.author: 6a5f89dafa3973ea
messages.subject: PCR fragment length normalization
parts:
Hi,

This question may be more specific for the Bengtsson et. al. 2008
paper. I'm not sure, but I think it will be fine to post it here
because it also regards the aroma.affymetrix normalization model.


I have read the paper and I wonder if the the Calculation of Raw copy
numbers eq(12) could accomodate
the fragment length correction eq(10).
And more importantly, the question is: Could the median itself eq(13)
as well compensate the Fragment length effect making the FLN step
redundant?
Maybe I'm missing something but the only problem I see in skipping the
FLN is that the median may not be robust enough to correct FL in the
presence of CN alteration on those probes.


Regarding the FLN implemented in the aroma.affymetrix for the SNP6.0
arrays is the same as in the paper?
I read the documentation and it says that it will be detailed in a
future paper, but I would like to know some
details now about the model ... :) if it is possible, a high level
description...

I will really appreciate your time and effort,

Roger,

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] PCR fragment length normalization
parts: Hi,

On Mon, Jul 14, 2008 at 5:39 PM, Roger <rpi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> This question may be more specific for the Bengtsson et. al. 2008
> paper. I'm not sure, but I think it will be fine to post it here
> because it also regards the aroma.affymetrix normalization model.
>
>
> I have read the paper and I wonder if the the Calculation of Raw copy
> numbers eq(12) could accomodate
> the fragment length correction eq(10).
> And more importantly, the question is: Could the median itself eq(13)
> as well compensate the Fragment length effect making the FLN step
> redundant?
> Maybe I'm missing something but the only problem I see in skipping the
> FLN is that the median may not be robust enough to correct FL in the
> presence of CN alteration on those probes.

your question is a valid question. In Eqn (10) of Bengtsson et al.
(2008), we write the fragment-length normalization as:

log2(theta*_ij) = log2(theta^_ij) - delta^_ij

where theta*_ij is the normalized chip effect for sample i=1,2,...,I
and locus/SNP/unit j=1,2,...,J. Continuing, theta^_ij is the
estimated chip effect (from the PLM), and delta^_ij is the estimated
fragment-length effect for that sample and that locus. Note that we
estimate the FL effect for each array, hence index 'i'.

So, to your point, when calculating the log-ratios as in Eqn (12);

M_ij = log2(theta*_ij / theta*_Rj) = log2(theta*_ij) - log2(theta*_Rj)

where theta*_Rj is the robust average of several samples, the FL
normalized data evaluates as:

M_ij = [log2(theta^_ij) - delta^_ij] - [log2(theta^_Rj) - delta^_Rj]
= [log2(theta^_ij/theta^_Rj) - [delta^_ij - delta^_Rj].

Note that *if and only if* fragment-length effect is the same for
sample 'i' and reference 'R', then delta^_ij - delta^_Rj == 0, and the
effect should cancel out.

However, whenever there is a small difference, then the
fragment-length effect will carry through to the log ratios. You can
see this yourself. If you plot log2(theta) versus fragment length and
draw a lowess or smooth spline through the data points you will find
that the longer fragments have less signal. You can see an example on
Page 'Calibration And Normalization Of Summarized Data'
[http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/calibration-and-normalization-of-summarized-data].
Now if you do this for many arrays, you will find that there are
small differences in the fitted curves across arrays.

To summarize: We do expect to see a fragment-length effect in our
theta:s - that is not strange and we do not remove that effect, we
only make the effect the same across all arrays (we normalize towards
the "target"). When we have made the effect the same for all arrays,
then it will cancel out as you suggest. One could of course generate
log ratios and normalize those (as in Nannya et al. 2005), but it more
practical to not bring in a reference until the very end.

>
>
> Regarding the FLN implemented in the aroma.affymetrix for the SNP6.0
> arrays is the same as in the paper?
> I read the documentation and it says that it will be detailed in a
> future paper, but I would like to know some
> details now about the model ... :) if it is possible, a high level
> description...

That work is still to be written up, but the issue with the newer GWS5
& GWS6 chip types is that DNA digested in parallel by two different
enzymes are hybridized to the same array. This means that the
observed signals are affected by two different fragment-length
effects. We use a simple mixture model to estimate the two effects
and correct for them. For simplicity you can think of extending Eqn
(10) so it has two delta^_ij terms.

Cheers

Henrik

>
> I will really appreciate your time and effort,
>
> Roger,

>

messages.author: 6a5f89dafa3973ea
messages.subject: Re: PCR fragment length normalization
parts:
Thanks Henrik,

I really appreciate your detailed answer.
I think now I understood well what is going on, FLN makes the PCR
effects the same but does not remove them.
In other words, it tries to remove the differences due to different
reaction conditions;then, the eq (12) would
remove the common PCR effect.

Regarding the FLN in GWS5&6. I think there are probes that are just on
Sty or Nsp fragments, and some that
are on both; so there will be probes with one and some with two
delta^_ij terms, is that correct?
I you could send me more detailed information if you have a draft or
anything, but don't worry if you can't send it.

Thank you very much again,

Roger,

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix]
parts:
Hi Stefano,

This is not an appropriate question for this list. However, I will do
my best to answer. Since your lab has its own Affymetrix platform,
can't you just contact the company who sold the system to you, since
it is usual for such companies to provide some technical
support/training? You could also contact Affymetrix directly for
support (contact details are easily accessible on their webpage).
From a quick google search I notice that the Field Application
Specialist for Italy is Alessandro Davassi so you could try to contact
him. Failing all of that, I would suggest trying to find other labs
in Italy (at first) who work with Affymetrix chips, and seeing if they
would be happy for you to visit to get some training.

Cheers,

Ken
